slide1_company_name.source: Edelweiss Financial Services Limited FY25 Annual Report

slide1_company_intro.value: Edelweiss Financial Services Limited (NSE: EDELWEISS | BSE: 532922), headquartered in Mumbai, is a diversified Indian financial services group operating across Alternative Asset Management (EAAA), Asset Reconstruction (EARCL), Mutual Funds (Edelweiss AMC), Life & General Insurance, and MSME/Housing Credit.
slide1_company_intro.source: Edelweiss Financial Services Limited FY25 Annual Report

slide1_brand_portfolio.value: Flagship franchises include EAAA (Edelweiss Alternative Asset Advisors, ₹59,000 Cr FPAUM), EARCL (India's leading Asset Reconstruction Company), Edelweiss Mutual Fund (₹1,41,000 Cr Total AAUM), Zuno General Insurance, and Nido Home Finance.
slide1_brand_portfolio.source: Edelweiss Financial Services Limited FY25 Annual Report

slide1_business_model.value: Transitioning from a balance-sheet-heavy wholesale lender into an asset-light, fee-driven Alternatives and Asset Management platform while systematically monetizing legacy wholesale credit assets to pay down corporate holding company debt.
slide1_business_model.source: Edelweiss Financial Services Limited FY25 Annual Report

slide1_product_ecosystem.value: Institutional private credit & infrastructure funds (EAAA), stressed asset resolution (EARCL), retail mutual funds & Bharat Bond ETF (Edelweiss AMC), digital auto/health insurance (Zuno), and agency life insurance (Edelweiss Tokio Life).
slide1_product_ecosystem.source: Edelweiss Financial Services Limited FY25 Annual Report

slide1_strategic_approach.value: Unlocking conglomerate value via stake monetization in EAAA, growing recurring management and fee income, and reducing consolidated borrowings (down from ₹46,148 Cr in FY19 to ₹18,004 Cr in FY25).
slide1_strategic_approach.source: Edelweiss Financial Services Limited FY25 Annual Report

slide2_company_name.source: Edelweiss Financial Services Limited FY25 Annual Report

slide2_executive_summary.value: In FY25, Edelweiss reported Consolidated Revenue from Operations of ₹9,393 Cr, Operating Profit Before Finance Costs of ₹3,360 Cr, Profit Before Tax of ₹802 Cr, and Consolidated Net Profit (PAT) of ₹536 Cr (EPS ₹5.67). Consolidated borrowings declined a further ₹2,354 Cr YoY to ₹18,004 Cr as wholesale book collections funded debt paydown.

slide2_thesis.value: Industrial FCFF is strictly excluded for Edelweiss because borrowings and loan repayments are operating raw material. Our SOTP values EAAA at 22.0x FY25 PAT (₹5,060 Cr), EARCL at 1.2x Book (₹3,360 Cr), Mutual Fund at 4.0% of AAUM (₹5,640 Cr), Insurance at 1.0x EV/Capital (₹1,500 Cr), and Credit at 0.8x Book (₹2,560 Cr), less -₹5,500 Cr Corporate HoldCo Net Debt (excluding ₹10,004 Cr operating credit debt already in P/B net worth), yielding ₹12,620 Cr Equity Value or ₹133.54/share (vs ₹108.00 snapshot CMP).

slide2_key_highlights.value:
• Methodological Boundary: Industrial FCFF strictly withheld; SOTP prevents double-counting operating credit debt
• EAAA Alternatives (₹230 Cr PAT @ 22.0x): ₹5,060 Cr | Edelweiss MF (4.0% of ₹1,41,000 Cr AAUM): ₹5,640 Cr
• EARCL ARC (₹2,800 Cr NW @ 1.2x): ₹3,360 Cr | Insurance (1.0x EV/Cap): ₹1,500 Cr
• NBFC & Housing Credit (₹3,200 Cr NW @ 0.8x): ₹2,560 Cr -> Gross Vertical Value ₹18,120 Cr
• Less Unallocated Corporate HoldCo Net Debt (-₹5,500 Cr) -> Equity Value ₹12,620 Cr (₹133.54 / share)

slide14_narrative.value: In financial services, positive Operating Cash Flow (₹3,384 Cr in FY25, ₹2,894 Cr in FY24) reflects intentional wholesale loan book collections and ARC recoveries, which directly fund Financing Cash Outflows (-₹4,828 Cr in FY25) to retire borrowings (down from ₹46,148 Cr in FY19 to ₹18,004 Cr in FY25).

slide16_company_name.source: Edelweiss Financial Services Limited FY25 Annual Report

slide16_current_ratio_narrative.value: Balance Sheet deleveraging is the defining financial trend: consolidated Debt-to-Equity improved from 6.01x in FY19 to 4.07x in FY25 as wholesale credit assets were harvested.

slide16_quick_ratio_narrative.value: Consolidated ROE recovered to 12.1% in FY25 as fee-generating verticals (EAAA and Mutual Fund) scaled and legacy credit provisions normalized.
